description: The pie chart illustrates the character distribution in the RoleplayPref dataset, organized into three primary categories—Virtual Characters, Real Characters, and Custom Characters—each subdivided into specific subcategories. The largest segment, Virtual Characters (light blue), encompasses five subcategories: Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters, collectively occupying the majority of the chart. Real Characters (light green) include seven subcategories: Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers, forming a moderately sized portion. Custom Characters (light pink) represent the smallest segment, with no further subdivisions shown. The chart uses distinct pastel colors for each primary category and its subcategories, with labels placed radially outside the pie. While percentages are not numerically labeled, the visual proportions suggest Virtual Characters dominate, followed by Real Characters, with Custom Characters comprising the smallest share. The structure reflects a hierarchical breakdown of character types used in role-playing language agent training, as referenced in the paper “ChARM: Character-based Act-adaptive Reward Modeling for Advanced Role-Playing Language Agents.”
